proposals.before: Early in Qianming Yang Yin, on Gao Yang dying instruction, stopped his vice directorship.
proposals.after: Early in Qianming Yang Yin, on Gao Yang's dying instruction, stopped his vice directorship.
proposals.reason: Missing possessive on "Gao Yang dying instruction"; Chinese 文宣遺旨 is Gao Yang's final instruction.

proposals.before: As advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting Prince of Guangning mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.
proposals.after: As advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting the Prince of Guangning's mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.
proposals.reason: "Prince of Guangning mansion" omits the possessive required for 廣寧王宅.

proposals.before: The rest who had signed were to be flogged too, but Zhao Yanshen seized the emperor sleeve in remonstrance and they were spared.
proposals.after: The rest who had signed were to be flogged too, but Zhao Yanshen insisted in remonstrance and they were spared.
proposals.reason: Chinese 執諫獲免 does not mention seizing the emperor's sleeve; the idiomatic rendering invents that detail.

proposals.before: After a long interval he was made governor of Jiao province, then transferred to regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, with salary from the two commanderies of Xinan and Heyin.
proposals.after: After a long interval he was made governor of Jiao province, then transferred to regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, with salary from the two commanderies of Xin'an and Heyin.
proposals.reason: "Xinan" should be "Xin'an" to match 新安 and the idiomatic spelling.

proposals.before: Later Prince of Nanan Sihao again charged the court with crimes, taking the harm done to Jishu and the others as his pretext, and summoned the brothers and nephews of the six men sons to follow the army toward Jinyang.
proposals.after: Later Prince of Nanan Sihao again charged the court with crimes, taking the harm done to Jishu and the others as his pretext, and summoned the brothers and nephews of the six men to follow the army toward Jinyang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六人兄弟子侄 means brothers and nephews of the six men; 'six men sons' is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: When the affair failed, Changjun and the rest were all killed with him; the six men wives were again taken into service in the palace.
proposals.after: When the affair failed, Changjun and the rest were all killed with him; the wives of the six men were again taken into service in the palace.
proposals.reason: 六人妻 means the wives of the six men, not 'six men wives'.

proposals.before: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Minister over the Masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing aunt, the great Princess of Boling.
proposals.after: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Minister over the Masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing's aunt, the great Princess of Boling.
proposals.reason: Missing possessive on 'Emperor Jing aunt' obscures that the princess was the emperor's aunt.

proposals.before: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former minister over the masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei emperor Jing aunt, the Princess of Boling the Great.
proposals.after: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former minister over the masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei Emperor Jing's aunt, the Great Princess of Boling.
proposals.reason: Awkward 'emperor Jing aunt' and reversed title obscure kinship and the princess's style.

proposals.before: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing province and appointed Ting army-camp staff officer opening a government office.
proposals.after: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing province and appointed Ting army-camp staff officer of an opened government office.
proposals.reason: 开府仓曹参军 names a kaifu army-camp staff post, not Ting himself opening an office.

proposals.before: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuan Kang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Ji, among others.
proposals.after: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuan Kang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Qu, among others.
proposals.reason: 季璩 is Qu/Ju, not Ji; the idiomatic spelling Ji Ji misreads 璩.

proposals.before: Ting knew how to make walnut oil for painting and offered it to the Prince of Changgang, saying, "Your Highness has the bones of an uncommon man. Xiao Zheng dreamed you rode a dragon into heaven."
proposals.after: Ting knew how to make walnut oil for painting and offered it to the Prince of Changguang, saying, "Your Highness has the bones of an uncommon man. I, Xiaozheng, dreamed you rode a dragon into heaven."
proposals.reason: 長廣 is Changguang, not Changgang; 孝徵 is Zu Ting's own courtesy name used in self-reference, not a separate person.

proposals.before: Ting now played to the throne and memorialized to posthumously honor Gao Huan as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Wenxuan's temple style to Weizong Jinglie Emperor. Wucheng was pleased and assented.
proposals.after: Ting now played to the throne and memorialized to posthumously honor the Grand Ancestor as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's temple style to Weizong Jinglie Emperor. Wucheng was pleased and assented.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 太祖獻武皇帝 and does not use the personal name Gao Huan in this unit; the idiomatic line invents that personal name.

proposals.before: Zhang Liang attended the heir in person, yet still needed the Four Whiteheads of Shang Mountain to settle Han's succession.
proposals.after: Zhang Liang attended the heir in person, yet still needed the Four Whiteheads to settle Han's succession.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 四皓; 'of Shang Mountain' is an interpretive addition not present in the source unit.

proposals.before: With Dame Lu he told the emperor, "Of Emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, not one son could take the throne. That the Present Sovereign still sits there is truly Ancestor Xiao Zheng's doing.
proposals.after: With Dame Lu he told the emperor, "Of Emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, not one son could take the throne. That the Present Sovereign still sits there is truly Zu Xiaozheng's doing.
proposals.reason: 祖孝徵 is the surname 祖 plus courtesy name 孝徵 (Zu Xiaozheng), not an honorific 'Ancestor'.

proposals.before: Together with Dame Lu he spoke to the emperor, saying, "Of the three emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, none of their sons could be enthroned; that the Present Sovereign still holds the imperial position is truly because of Ancestor Xiao Zheng.
proposals.after: Together with Dame Lu he spoke to the emperor, saying, "Of the three emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, none of their sons could be enthroned; that the Present Sovereign still holds the imperial position is truly because of Zu Xiaozheng.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 祖孝徵 is Zu Xiaozheng, not Ancestor Xiao Zheng.

proposals.before: After He Shikai died he again urged Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and made Ting attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.after: After He Shikai died, Ting again urged Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and was made attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.reason: Silent subject after 和士開死後 is Ting persuading Dame Lu; English 'he...made Ting' wrongly makes the same subject both persuader and appointing authority over himself.

proposals.before: Zu Ting had heard him plainly enough. With the empress out of favor, he carried the verse to the emperor: "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; bright moon shines on Chang'an."
proposals.after: Zu Ting had heard him plainly enough. Because Guang's daughter the empress was out of favor, he carried the verse to the emperor: "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; bright moon shines on Chang'an."
proposals.reason: Chinese 因其女皇後無寵 identifies the empress as Hulü Guang's daughter; the idiomatic omits 其女 and loses that link.

proposals.before: He said "the blind old man" meant himself — one who shared the state's weal and woe — and pressed the emperor to move. "The meddlesome old woman," he said, was Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu of the Way.
proposals.after: He said "the blind old man" meant himself — one who shared the state's weal and woe — and pressed the emperor to move. He said "the meddlesome old woman" pointed to Female Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Lu clan.
proposals.reason: 道 here marks identification/saying, not a place or 'the Way'; 女侍中陸氏 is Female Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu.

proposals.before: Ting also said that "the blind old man" was himself, that he shared the state's joy and sorrow, and urged the emperor to act; he said that "the meddlesome old woman" resembled Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu of the Way.
proposals.after: Ting also said that "the blind old man" was himself, that he shared the state's joy and sorrow, and urged the emperor to act; he said that "the meddlesome old woman" pointed to Female Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Lu clan.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 道…女侍中陸氏 as 'of the Way' instead of identifying Female Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu.

proposals.before: Still fearing the Later Sovereign was drowning in favorites, he sought backing from the empress's kin: he asked that her elder brother Hu Junyu be made attendant-in-ordinary and central commander of the guards, and summoned Junyu's brother Junbi, governor of Liang Province, intending to make him vice director of the censorate.
proposals.after: Still fearing the Later Sovereign was drowning in favorites, he sought backing from the empress's kin: he asked that her elder brother Hu Junyu be made attendant-in-ordinary and central commander of the guards, and summoned Junyu's elder brother Junbi, governor of Liang Province, intending to make him vice director of the censorate.
proposals.reason: Chinese 君瑜兄 marks Junbi as Junyu's elder brother; idiomatic drops 'elder'.

proposals.before: His compositions did not match his brother's, yet he was quick-witted and eloquent and understood music.
proposals.after: His compositions did not match his elder brother's, yet he was quick-witted and eloquent and understood music.
proposals.reason: Source 兄 marks elder brother; the idiomatic 'brother's' drops that seniority, which the literal correctly keeps as 'elder brother's'.

decisions.reason: 文宣遺旨 is Gao Yang's (Wenxuan's) final instruction; the missing possessive makes the literal ungrammatical and obscures that relation.
詣廣寧王宅 means visiting the Prince of Guangning's mansion; the original omits the required possessive.
執諫獲免 records only that Zhao Yanshen remonstrated and they were spared; seizing the emperor's sleeve is invented and correctly removed.
新安 is Xin'an; unapostrophized Xinan misrepresents the place name and mismatches the idiomatic spelling.
六人兄弟子侄 means the brothers and nephews of the six men; 'six men sons' invents a nonexistent kinship node.
六人妻 means the wives of the six men; 'six men wives' is ungrammatical and misreads the genitive.
魏孝靜帝姑 marks the princess as Emperor Jing's aunt; the missing possessive obscures that kinship.

decisions.reason: 魏孝靜帝姑博陵長公主 requires Emperor Jing's aunt and Great Princess of Boling; the original reverses the title and drops the possessive.

decisions.after: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing province and appointed Ting as army-camp staff officer of an opened government office.
decisions.reason: 開府倉曹參軍 is a kaifu army-camp staff post title, not Ting opening an office; the proposal corrects the sense but still needs 'as' for natural English.
季璩 is Ji Qu (璩 = Qu/Ju); idiomatic 'Ji Ji' misreads the given name.
長廣王 is Prince of Changguang, and 孝徵 is Zu Ting's own courtesy name in self-reference, not a third party Xiao Zheng.

decisions.after: Ting now played to the throne and memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor Emperor Xianwu as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's temple style to Weizong Jinglie Emperor. Wucheng was pleased and assented.
decisions.reason: The unit has 太祖獻武皇帝, not the personal name Gao Huan; the proposal rightly drops that invention but still omits 獻武, which belongs in the repaired English.

decisions.reason: The unit has only 四皓; 'of Shang Mountain' is an interpretive gloss not present in the Chinese.
祖孝徵 is surname 祖 plus courtesy name 孝徵 (Zu Xiaozheng), not an honorific 'Ancestor'.
Same naming error as the idiomatic: 祖孝徵 is Zu Xiaozheng, not Ancestor Xiao Zheng.
After 和士開死後 the silent subject of 說陸媼 is Ting, and 以珽為侍中 is Ting's appointment; the original wrongly makes one agent both persuader and appointing authority over himself.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 仍說陸媼出彥深，以珽為侍中

decisions.reason: 因其女皇後無寵 identifies the empress as Hulü Guang's daughter; omitting 其女 loses that kinship link.

decisions.after: He said "the blind old man" meant himself — one who shared the state's weal and woe — and pressed the emperor to move. He said "the meddlesome old woman" seemed to point to Female Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Lu clan.
decisions.reason: 似道女侍中陸氏 means the verse seemed to point to Female Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Lu clan; 'of the Way' is wrong, and the proposal's 'pointed to' drops 似.

decisions.after: Ting also said that "the blind old man" was himself, that he shared the state's joy and sorrow, and urged the emperor to act; he said that "the meddlesome old woman" seemed to point to Female Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Lu clan.
decisions.reason: Same mistranslation of 似道女侍中陸氏; keep 似 while correcting 'of the Way' and restoring 女侍中.
君瑜兄 marks Junbi as Junyu's elder brother; dropping 'elder' loses the seniority the source states.

decisions.reason: 不逮兄 compares Xiaoyin to his elder brother; the idiomatic 'brother's' drops that seniority.

claimRetractions.reason: s0132 names 太祖獻武皇帝, not the personal name 高歡; that personal-name claim was created solely by the bad idiomatic rendering.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted repair corrects the English personal name from misread Ji Ji to Ji Qu for 季璩.
Accepted repair restores courtesy name Xiaozheng for 孝徵 rather than spaced Xiao Zheng.
Accepted repair corrects 長廣王 to Prince of Changguang.
Accepted repair shows 其女皇後 explicitly identifies the empress as Guang's daughter, so certainty rises from strongly-inferred to explicit.
